mutations.because: Removing the `existsSync` guard before `openResult` lets the result reach `open(path, "wx")`, which throws EEXIST into the apply catch block — a different error than the `describeResultRefusal` refusal. Title 11 exits 1 on both baseline and mutant, but the error line changes from the 'already exists' refusal to the EEXIST message, caught on `expect(err[0]).toBe(...)` at apply.test.ts:450.
command: apply refuses a result path that already exists

mutations.because: Writing each campaign line from position 0 instead of the current position overwrites earlier lines, violating N4/D229. Title 16's `expect(writes.every((c) => c.length === 3)).toBe(true)` fails on the mutant because the position argument makes each write call pass 4 args (buf, offset, length, position) instead of 3.
command: the result file is appended one line per campaign and never rewritten

mutations.because: Removing the try around the step lets a thrown error abort the run instead of recording it as refused+partial, violating N8b2. The step throws at apply.test.ts:1061, propagating through applyCampaigns at apply.ts:225; the test fails before reaching `expect(step).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`.
command: a step that throws is recorded as refused and partial and the next campaign still runs

mutations.because: Mutant drops the `dir.sync()` call, so `openResult` can hand back a file handle whose parent-directory entry was never fsynced: a crash can leave the campaigns written but the result path gone (N4/D229). Baseline calls `dir.sync()` once, caught by `openResult syncs the parent directory after creating the file`.
command: openResult syncs the parent directory after creating the file
